You are asking the wrong question. More precisely, you are asking the right question at the wrong time.

Rather than asking "how do I stop feeling guilty" you should be asking "WHY do I feel guilty".

I can't answer that for you. No one here can answer that for you.

You need to take some time and reflect. Are you feeling guilty because you feel you aren't living up to society's expectations of you? Do you feel guilty because you were raised to behave a different way? Do you feel guilty because you do not want to live this way? There is some conflict between what you are doing, what you are achieving, and what you think others expect of you or what you expect of yourself. It is the gap between those conflicting expectations, actions, and results that the guilt is rising up from.

Once you have identified the conflict then you can seek resolution. However, that resolution will require change, and you will have to determine what sacrifices you are willing to make to achieve resolution.

Taking anyone else's advice without understanding yourself first is likely to cause you more problems down the line. Even if your decision is to continue with the same behavior, achieving the same results, and learning to cope with the guilt for the time being, that very well may be the best solution... for you.

Take some time, sit in a quiet place with few distractions (maybe a nice bottle of wine) and figure it out for yourself.

Sex has been a very intimate thing for you in the past and it's something that you held close to you and your partners. This could just be a different gear in your life that you're experiencing cause the person you are right now might not be the person you'll be 5 years down the road.

You're at an impasse of ideals right now but there's a way through and only you can decide which route is best.
